title: The King's Missing Royal Mustache (PT)
summary: Akbar plays a practical joke on his ministers by claiming a hair of his mustache was plucked in the night. Birbal's reaction exposes courtly psychology.
full_text:
Emperor Akbar was in a playful and observant mood one morning in the Diwan-i-Khas. Stroking his magnificent royal mustache, he looked at his assembled ministers with a stern, solemn countenance and said:

'My lords! A shocking treason was committed inside my private bedchamber last night! Someone crept beside my bed while I slept and plucked a hair directly from my royal mustache! What punishment should be inflicted upon this brazen villain?'

The courtiers, eager to demonstrate their ferocious loyalty, shouted with competitive fury:

'Sire! He should be boiled in oil!' shouted the chief general.

'He should be fed to wild dogs!' proclaimed the treasurer.

'He should be tied to the mouth of a cannon and blown to pieces!' roared the magistrate.

Birbal, who had been sitting calmly in his chair, remained silent, a gentle smile playing upon his lips.

Akbar looked at him: 'Birbal, why do you not propose a punishment? Are you not outraged by the insult to your Emperor's mustache?'

Birbal bowed with serene dignity:

'Your Majesty, I propose that the person who pulled your royal hair be given a handful of sweet sugar candy and a warm kiss upon his forehead!'

The courtiers gasped in horror. 'Treason!' muttered the general. 'Birbal insults the Emperor!'

Akbar smiled: 'Explain yourself, Birbal.'

Birbal laughed softly:

'Sire, who in all the vast territories of Hindustan could ever get close enough to Your Majesty's face while you slept, without being speared by fifty armed guards, except for your little infant grandson, Prince Khurram, who sleeps beside your pillow?

'Only an innocent baby would dare pull the Emperor's mustache, and for a child, sweetmeats and kisses are the only fitting response!'

Akbar laughed with joy, embracing Birbal: 'You know my heart better than all my ministers! It was indeed my little grandson who pulled my mustache this morning!'

Akbar looked at the other ministers and warned them that those who are quick to demand blood and torture reveal only the cruelty of their own hearts.
